name: Marmaris Theme Blog Editor
author: marmaristheme

sections.description:
Marmaris Theme Blog Editor adds a simpler writing layer to the native WordPress Block Editor while keeping WordPress as the content and publishing authority.

Compatibility commitments:

  • WordPress Core remains the content and publishing authority.
  • The Gutenberg plugin is optional.
  • The plugin uses native WordPress blocks and no proprietary document format.
  • Marmaris Theme Blog Editor includes Visual and Code views; Code view edits native WordPress block markup and validates it before applying changes.
  • Rank Math and Yoast keep ownership of their SEO data and editor workflows.
  • Deactivation leaves native content usable.

Privacy

Marmaris Theme Blog Editor does not send post content, writing statistics, plugin inventory, or editor activity to Marmaris Theme. V1 contains no telemetry and no remote authoring service.

Content Portability

The plugin uses native WordPress blocks and publishing data. V1 registers no custom content blocks and no shortcode document format.

More Tools

The plugin may show optional separate Marmaris Theme products such as Core Optimizer and Fast Safe Cache. They are not required, are not installed automatically, and clicks are not tracked by Marmaris Theme Blog Editor.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Marmaris Theme Blog Editor.
  3. Continue using the native WordPress editor.
sections.faq:
Does Apply Changes save my post?

Apply Changes returns the workspace draft to WordPress. Use the native Save, Update or Publish action to save it. Unapplied workspace edits are not separately autosaved.

What if verification fails or the document changed?

Keep your work open and check the connection/session before retrying Apply. Each check stops after 15 seconds. If the document changed, preserve all unsaved work before reloading WordPress and reviewing the latest saved version. See documentation/index.html for recovery and support instructions.

Does this replace Gutenberg?

No. It enhances the native WordPress Block Editor.

Is the Gutenberg plugin required?

No.

Does the plugin own my content?

No. Native WordPress content remains the authority.

  • Fixed Text Color and Highlight so selected text receives native inline core/text-color formatting, while an unselected paragraph/heading receives block-level color.
  • Preserved the active block/text selection while opening the heading and color dropdowns.

0.9.33

  • Made the modal content container fill the available height and added an accessible drag handle for resizing the editor workspace vertically.

  • Blocked stale tabs at workspace opening and limited verification requests to 15 seconds.
  • Added native RichTextData support to formatting, document statistics and workspace routing.
  • Kept workspace Undo/Redo within the isolated draft using the WordPress history utility.
  • Added a scoped browser warning for unapplied workspace changes.
  • Fixed link rel parsing and preserved existing link attributes.

  • Replaces Classic block edit UI only inside the plugin workspace with a structure-preserving placeholder; selecting Edit Classic content switches the same modal into the isolated Classic editor and Back to blocks returns to Gutenberg.
  • Supports multiple and nested core/freeform blocks through a scoped public editor.BlockEdit filter while leaving the normal WordPress editor untouched.
  • Preserves the dirty-close, public launcher, Classic adapter, safe cloning and stale-document protections.

0.9.24

  • Reworked cross-tab stale-document protection so the baseline is captured from the authoritative WordPress REST response when Marmaris Theme Blog Editor opens, instead of relying on the current tab’s local editor snapshot.
  • Rechecks the same post through a cache-bypassed, read-only WordPress REST request on Apply Changes and compares saved content plus modified timestamps before any write.
  • Fails safely if the server baseline or freshness check cannot be verified, and preserves behavior.

0.9.23

  • Extended stale-document protection beyond the local Gutenberg store by verifying the current saved WordPress content through the native authenticated REST API only when Apply Changes is pressed.
  • Detects edits saved in another browser/tab while the workspace is open and blocks Apply instead of allowing an older snapshot to overwrite newer content.
  • Keeps the check read-only, scoped to the current post, limited to id and content, and fails safely if WordPress cannot verify the latest saved document.
  • Preserves dirty-close, Classic adapter, public Gutenberg launcher, safe cloning and WordPress Save/Update/Publish ownership.

0.9.22

  • Added a canonical block-document fingerprint at Marmaris Theme Blog Editor open time and rechecks the live WordPress block tree before Apply Changes.
  • Refuses Apply Changes if the WordPress block document changed while the workspace was open, preventing an older modal snapshot from silently overwriting newer content.
  • Pins the workspace route/source to the opening document while keeping live fingerprint observation outside the nested editor provider; Classic and Gutenberg paths both fail safely without changing canonical content.
  • Preserves dirty-close, Classic adapter, public Gutenberg launcher, safe cloning and WordPress Save/Update/Publish ownership.

0.9.21

  • Removed the shallow-copy block fallback from the Gutenberg workspace. If WordPress block serialization/parsing cannot produce an isolated copy, the workspace now fails safely without touching canonical content.
  • Revalidates the edited block tree before Apply Changes and refuses the write if a safe clone cannot be created, leaving the draft open and canonical WordPress content unchanged.
  • Preserves the accepted Classic adapter, dirty-close lifecycle, public Gutenberg launcher and WordPress save/publish ownership.

0.9.20

  • Restored reliable Escape handling after Classic adapter isolation by binding the scoped handler at both TinyMCE and iframe-document levels.
  • Rebinds the iframe-document listener when the Classic editor regains focus, and removes all adapter-owned Escape/focus listeners during cleanup.
  • Preserves the existing dirty-close confirmation, Apply Changes behavior, public Gutenberg launcher, and WordPress save/publish ownership.
